what: The one grammar for `?startapp=` deep-link payloads, read by both implementations.
why: - `startapp` is Telegram's parameter and Telegram constrains it, the parser and the emitter live in different languages (TypeScript in web/src/telegram/startapp.ts, Python in packages/polygm_core/telegrambot/channel.py), and the failure mode of a disagreement is silent: the emitter mints a link, the parser rejects it, and a channel alert's trade button lands on 'that link did not look right'. Both sides read this file in their own test suite, so a change to one that is not a change to both fails a build rather than a customer.
charset_note: The literal character set, spelled out — NOT a regex class. The first version of this file wrote it as 'A-Za-z0-9_.-' and the TypeScript side read it as a class (correct) while the Python side read it as a list of literal characters (also, in isolation, a defensible reading) — so `fed-cut-sept` filtered down to `--` and every channel deep link would have opened an empty market. One representation, unambiguous in both languages: regex users build a class from it and escape `-`, set users build a set from it. No colon: Telegram's `startapp` value is a short URL-safe token, so anything outside this set is percent-encoded by a client at best.
